The official and national language is [Dhivehi](/wiki/Maldivian_language "Maldivian language"), an [Indo-Aryan language](/wiki/Indo-Aryan_languages "Indo-Aryan languages") closely related to the [Sinhala language](/wiki/Sinhala_language "Sinhala language") of Sri Lanka. The first known script used to write Dhivehi is the *[eveyla akuru](/wiki/Eveyla_akuru "Eveyla akuru")* script, which is found in the historical recording of kings (*raadhavalhi*). Later a script called *[Dhives Akuru](/wiki/Dhives_Akuru "Dhives Akuru")* was used for a long period. The present-day script is called [Thaana](/wiki/Thaana "Thaana") and is written from right to left. [Thaana](/wiki/Thaana "Thaana") is derived from a mix of the old indigenous script of [Dhives Akuru](/wiki/Dhives_Akuru "Dhives Akuru") and [Arabic abjad](/wiki/Arabic_script "Arabic script"). Thaana is said to have been introduced during the reign of [Mohamed Thakurufaanu](/wiki/Muhammad_Thakurufaanu_al-Auzam "Muhammad Thakurufaanu al-Auzam").

Nanjing University's motto is "Sincerity with Aspiration, Perseverance with Integrity" (simplified Chinese: 诚朴雄伟 励学敦行; traditional Chinese: 誠樸雄偉 勵學敦行; pinyin: *chéng pǔ xióng wěi lì xué dūn xíng*).[[10]](#cite_note-nju_motto-10)[[11]](#cite_note-nju_motto_chinese-11) The first part of the motto, "Sincerity with Aspiration," originated during the university's period as the historical National Central University, while "Perseverance with Integrity" draws inspiration from classical Chinese aphorisms.[[12]](#cite_note-nju_motto_history_xiaobao-12)

Historically, [Li Ruiqing](/wiki/Li_Ruiqing "Li Ruiqing"), president of Liangjiang Higher Normal School, the precursor to Nanjing University, inscribed the motto "One who chews on the roots of vegetables can accomplish great things" (Chinese: 嚼得菜根 做得大事; pinyin: *jiáo dé cài gēn zuò dé dà shì*).[[12]](#cite_note-nju_motto_history_xiaobao-12) Later, during the National Central University era, President [Luo Jialun](/wiki/Luo_Jialun "Luo Jialun") formally adopted "Sincerity with Aspiration" as the university's motto. Following the establishment of the People's Republic of China in 1949, Nanjing University underwent a series of reorganizations and consolidations, and a formal motto was not established for an extended period.[[12]](#cite_note-nju_motto_history_xiaobao-12) The current motto, "Sincerity with Aspiration, Perseverance with Integrity", was adopted during the university's centennial celebration in 2002 under the leadership of then-President [Jiang Shusheng](/wiki/Jiang_Shusheng "Jiang Shusheng"), following extensive consultation with faculty and students.[[13]](#cite_note-nju_motto_jiangshusheng-13)

The school song of Nanjing University was composed in 1916 and originally served as the school song of Nanjing Higher Normal School, with the lyrics written by [Jiang Qian](/wiki/Jiang_Qian "Jiang Qian") and melody composed by [Li Shutong](/wiki/Li_Shutong "Li Shutong") (Hong Yi).[[14]](#cite_note-nju_song-14)

In the 25th annual *Forbes* list of global billionaires, Slim added $20.5 billion to his fortune, the most of anyone, and retained his number one ranking with a total fortune of $74 billion. Gates remained in second place with $56 billion, while Warren Buffett was third with $50 billion. The top 10 had a combined wealth of $406 billion, up from $342 billion in 2010. According to *Forbes* editor Kerry Dolan, "media and technology billionaires definitely benefited from a stronger stock market and a growing enthusiasm for all things social" since the 2010 list.[[40]](#cite_note-Hollywood2011-40) However, Nigerian commodity mogul Aliko Dangote was the greatest gainer on a percentage basis as his fortune increased 557 percent to $13.5 billion. Mark Zuckerberg was one of seven Facebook-related billionaires on the list, as he added $9.5 billion to his net worth to move up to 52nd. Facebook co-founder [Dustin Moskovitz](/wiki/Dustin_Moskovitz "Dustin Moskovitz") was the youngest person on the list. Aged 26, eight days younger than Zuckerberg, he debuted at number 420 with an estimated fortune of $2.7 billion. [IKEA](/wiki/IKEA "IKEA") founder [Ingvar Kamprad](/wiki/Ingvar_Kamprad "Ingvar Kamprad") was the largest loser as he saw his fortune plummet from $23 billion to $6 billion, dropping him from 11th to 162nd overall.

A record 1,210 billionaires made the 2011 list, representing a combined wealth of $4.5 trillion, up from $3.6 trillion the previous year.[[41]](#cite_note-Syracuse2011-41) One third of the world's billionaires, 413, came from the United States. China had the second most billionaires with 115, while Russia was third with 101. Asia moved up to 332 billionaires, passing Europe as a region for the first time since the 1990s. The 2011 list included 214 newcomers and the average net worth of those on it increased to $3.7 billion.[[40]](#cite_note-Hollywood2011-40)
